fun_facts: Newly hatched spadefish don't swim upright: for their first weeks they drift on their sides near the surface, black and white and mottled, an almost perfect impression of a dead leaf floating in the current.
Despite looking like a reef fish out of the angelfish family, a spadefish isn't closely related to one at all; the disc shape and vertical bars are convergent evolution, not shared ancestry.

A single wreck or reef can hold a spadefish school hundreds strong, tight enough that divers sometimes follow the moving wall of fish, not the structure itself, to find their way back to the anchor line.
